# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** 45  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Lavendar is a little lady with snow-white, thick, wavy hair arranged in puffs and coils. Beneath her hair is a fresh, girlish face with pink cheeks, dimples, sweet lips, and big, soft, wood-brown eyes with golden glints. Her voice sounds like white satin, tinkling water, and fairy bells. She wears a dainty gown of cream muslin patterned with pale-hued roses.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c27 P58](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0058), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029)_

## Personality

Imaginative and fond of pretending, Miss Lavendar loves playing at tea parties and keeping up imagined worlds to compensate for her lonely life. She is exceptionally sweet, hospitable, and a good listener who charms those around her. Although she generally dislikes being kissed, she feels a special warmth and connection toward young friends who share her imaginative nature. When troubled, she can become quiet, tired, and withdrawn.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c23 P34](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0034), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c27 P51](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0051)_

## History

Miss Lavendar lived a quiet, retired life at Echo Lodge. Ten years after her mother's death, she took in a series of young girls from the Bowman family to assist her and keep her company, calling each of them 'Charlotta' in turn. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited her one autumn afternoon and were immediately welcomed into her home for tea. A deep friendship grew between Anne and Miss Lavendar, bringing joy and companionship into her quiet life. Later, when Stephen Irving returned and re-entered her life, the two reconciled their past quarrel. They were married in a ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor in late August, surrounded by friends, before planning to travel and reside together in Boston.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c29 P4](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0004), [v2 c30 P0](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0000), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he loved the scent after staying in a lavender-scented bed at her mother's family home in East Grafton  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Her mother planted lavender borders in her garden long ago  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Her mother died ten years ago, leading her to hire young Charlotta Bowman for company and work  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Was engaged twenty-five years ago to Stephen Irving, but they quarreled and broke off the engagement  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>

## Quotes

> But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you.  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049)</sub>

> But what is the use of being an independent old maid if you can’t be silly when you want to, and when it doesn’t hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> I’m going to give you girls a bunch of lavendar apiece,” said Miss Lavendar brightly, as if she had not heard the answer to her question. “It’s very sweet, don’t you think? Mother always loved it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> Oh, sometimes, I think it is of no use to make friends. They only go out of your life after awhile and leave a hurt that is worse than the emptiness before they came.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>
